ladakh.overview: Ladakh is a high-altitude desert of stark, jagged peaks and deep valleys, offering dramatic Himalayan trekking. The classic route is the Markha Valley trek, a multi-day journey crossing passes over 16,000 feet past remote villages and Buddhist monasteries. Day hikers can tackle steep acclimatization trails around Leh, which sits at about 11,500 feet, or explore the Sham Valley. The season is short, dictated by snow on the high passes, with the best hiking from June to September.

months.8: The best time for high-altitude trekking. Trails are clear, and the dramatic desert scenery is at its most accessible, though the intense sun above 11,000 feet requires an early start.

months.1: January rains make the Pipiwai Trail muddy and waterfalls heavy, while Haleakalā can be cold and windy at 10,000 feet.
months.3: Trails begin to dry out slightly, though the bamboo forest remains slick and Haleakalā requires warm layers at its 10,000-foot rim.
months.8: The warmest temperatures demand early starts for any long crater hikes, as the sun at 10,000 feet is intense.

peru.overview: Cusco and the Sacred Valley feature famous trekking, leading through the high Andes to ancient ruins. The multi-day routes are the main draw, led by the four-day Inca Trail to Machu Picchu, which needs a permit booked months ahead, and the demanding Salkantay trek, over a pass of about 15,000 feet, past glacier-capped peaks. Day hikers can tackle the steep climb to Rainbow Mountain at over 16,000 feet, or explore shorter paths between Inca sites. The best conditions run from May to September, while heavy rains disrupt routes early in the year.

months.11: The clear skies continue, keeping the spectacular mountain views sharp. The air grows cold, especially on passes above 13,000 feet, but the major treks remain open and excellent.

Trekking conditions stay superb, with crisp, cloudless skies and dry trails across the entire network. Temperatures drop steadily as winter approaches, making the tea houses above 14,000 feet very cold at night.

months.1: Winter brings prime walking conditions with mild temperatures and clear skies. Trails through the Anaga mountains and Garajonay are lush and green, while the high routes on Mount Teide, which tops 12,188 feet, remain cool and exposed.

months.1: The dry winter weather provides clear skies and excellent visibility for the demanding ascent of Iztaccíhuatl, though temperatures on the 17,000-foot summit are freezing.
